title: Dynamically suppressing cavity dephasing induced by frequency fluctuations of a coupled nonlinear mode
authors: Yunwei Lu, Xinyuan You, Ziwen Huang, Sébastien Léger, Jens Koch, Yao Lu
abstract: High-coherence superconducting cavities offer a promising platform for quantum information, with long coherence times and negligible intrinsic dephasing. However, cavity control generally relies on nonlinear Josephson elements whose frequency fluctuations are inherited by the cavity as dephasing, potentially limiting control fidelities and eroding the noise bias used in error-correction protocols. Here, we introduce Stark-Assisted Flux-noise Evasion (SAFE), a hardware-efficient protocol that protects the cavity from inherited dephasing using only a weak off-resonant microwave drive applied to the nonlinear element. As a concrete setup, we analyze a 3D superconducting cavity dispersively coupled to a flux-tunable transmon (FTT) subject to $1/f$ flux noise. Analytical predictions are confirmed by Monte Carlo simulations with realistic parameters, which show that SAFE can extend the cavity dephasing time by more than an order of magnitude while keeping residual drive-induced decoherence subdominant.
summary: This paper introduces a protocol called SAFE to protect superconducting cavities from dephasing caused by flux noise inherent in nonlinear Josephson elements. By applying a weak off-resonant microwave drive, the system can be tuned to a dynamical sweet spot where the cavity frequency becomes insensitive to low-frequency noise. This significantly enhances coherence times, improving fidelity for quantum control applications.
main_problem: The primary challenge addressed is mitigating cavity dephasing caused by low-frequency flux noise originating from coupled nonlinear Josephson elements.
main_result: The proposed Stark-Assisted Flux-noise Evasion (SAFE) protocol successfully creates a dynamical sweet spot, extending the cavity dephasing time by over an order of magnitude.
method: The authors use Floquet theory and master equation analysis to derive conditions for noise insensitivity, implementing operator transformations and secular approximations.
model_or_system: The system modeled is a superconducting microwave cavity dispersively coupled to a flux-tunable transmon (FTT), analyzed under the influence of $1/f$ flux noise.
key_observables: Cavity dephasing time ($T_2^*$), susceptibility ($D_{n,m}$), and residual decoherence rates.
important_parameters: Weak off-resonant microwave drive strength ($\Omega_0$), detuning ($\Delta_{bc}$), and the noise spectral density ($S_{1/f}(\omega)$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on weak driving approximations, dispersive coupling regimes, and truncating the system dynamics to a manageable subspace.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the creation of dynamical sweet spots in parameter space (Fig. 2) and show how the drive compensates for noise-induced shifts.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from identifying the noise source and its effect on the Hamiltonian, to deriving the condition for a dynamical sweet spot using Floquet theory, and finally modeling the dynamics via an effective master equation incorporating the protective drive.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses decoherence mitigation in superconducting quantum circuits by engineering noise resilience through external driving fields, which is central to modern quantum information processing architectures.

The first logical qubit is encoded in cavities c1 and c3, and the second logical qubit is encoded in cavities c2 and c4. The rails c1 and c2, one from each dual- rail qubit, are dispersively coupled to a common flux-tunable transmon (FTT) ancilla with respective coupling strengths g(1) and g(2) and detunings ∆(1) bc and ∆(2) bc . Flux fluctuations δΦ(t) modulate the FTT frequency and induce correlated fre- quency fluctuations in the coupled cavity rails through the dispersive Lamb shift.
